A vast wizard's library occupying a cathedral-vaulted nave, its ribbed stone ceiling lost in shadow above tier upon tier of iron-railed galleries sagging beneath centuries of leather-bound tomes. Cracked mosaic floors depict constellations worn smooth by generations of boots. Brass reading-globes hang on tarnished chains between warped oak shelves. Dust motes drift through narrow lancet windows, and the smell of aged vellum saturates every stone.

A throne hall of immense depth, its central aisle flanked by twin rows of basalt columns rising to pointed arches carved with the heraldry of a dozen conquered dynasties. A raised dais dominates the far wall, supporting a single iron throne blackened with age. Moth-eaten banners hang from corbels overhead, and the flagstone approach is grooved by centuries of processions into shallow parallel ruts.

An inner castle courtyard enclosed on four sides by colonnaded walkways, a cracked fountain at its center still trickling mineral-stained water into a green-filmed basin. Stained-glass panels set into arched roof sections overhead cast fractured colored light across worn cobblestones. Climbing vines have crept between stone joints for decades, and the colonnade capitals are thick with carved foliage darkened by weather and age.

A soaring spiral stairwell climbing the interior of an ancient tower, its broad stone steps worn concave at their centers by uncountable ascents. Iron chandeliers loaded with burned-down candle stumps hang at each landing on chains that creak in the updraft. Carved stone balustrades are chipped and mended with iron staples. Lancet windows at intervals spill long diagonal light across steps green with lichen near the sill-stones.

A dragon-hoard vault of enormous breadth, its barrel-vaulted ceiling supported by massive pillars encrusted with riveted iron bands. The floor is submerged under a rolling sea of gold coins, gem-set cups, crowns, and tarnished armor to knee-depth, disturbed into ridges and hollows as though by enormous shifting weight. Heavy iron doors with multiple lock-bars line the far wall, their hinges rust-streaked, their lock-plates scratched raw by centuries of forced entry attempts.

A domed observatory chamber of cathedral proportions, its vast coffered dome perforated by a ring of circular windows aligned with specific stellar positions. Concentric rings of rune-carved stone tile the floor, polished by centuries of ritual use to a dull gleam. A massive bronze orrery at the room's center has seized at an angle, its gears fused by oxidation. Crumbling star-charts in gilded frames line the curved walls between the windows.

A dwarven forge-cathedral with a multi-tiered interior, its soaring vaulted ceiling blackened by ages of smoke rising from channels of sluggish molten rock threading the floor below. Iron walkways at three levels connect stone platforms around the central forge-pit, their grating warped by heat. Enormous bellows mechanisms of riveted leather hang idle from overhead chains. Hammered-metal friezes depicting ancestral smithing deeds line the upper walls, each panel tarnished to near-invisibility.

A ritual summoning hall with a vast hexagonal chamber, its floor consuming a single enormous circle inlaid in silver and pale stone, the silver tarnished dark between its carved channels. Six side-altars occupy recessed alcoves around the perimeter, each fitted with cracked stone pedestals bearing cold censer-bowls. The vaulted ceiling above the circle is scorched in a broad upward bloom of char. Iron brackets on the walls hold empty torch-sconces worn smooth by handling.

A long banquet hall with a coffered oak ceiling hanging low over twin rows of trestle tables stretching its full length, the wood darkened and grease-stained by centuries of feasts. Three great hearths line each long wall, their mantels carved with hunting scenes nearly obscured by soot. Faded tapestries between the hearths depict battles already half-forgotten. Tallow candles cluster in iron candelabras spaced along the tables, their bases buried under generations of dripped wax.

A war-council chamber dominated by a relief-map table spanning most of its floor, carved from a single slab of pale granite to show mountain ranges, rivers, and city-markers worn smooth where countless hands have pointed. Heavy timber roof beams cross overhead, hung with rows of campaign banners faded to indistinct color. Arrow-slit windows in the thick walls cast thin bright lines across the map. Iron brackets hold extinguished oil-lamps at each wall corner.

A portal hall of grand proportions, its arched nave lined on both sides with seven permanent gate-frames of dressed black stone, each tall enough to admit a mounted rider. The floor between them is a worn mosaic of directional runes, the grout cracked and refilled multiple times with different-colored mortar. The vaulted ceiling is stained directly above each frame by the residue of ten thousand activations. Chains and iron rings anchor each frame to the floor and walls.

A magical temple-basilica with rune-carved walls covering every surface in layered script accumulated over centuries, later inscriptions cut directly over earlier ones until the stone reads as a palimpsest of overlapping intention. Floating stone circles of diminishing size ascend above the central altar toward the vaulted apex, their levitation unsteady after ages of ambient disruption. Rows of cracked pillar-candles on iron stands crowd the side-aisles. Mosaic floor panels depicting mythic scenes are missing tesserae in scattered patches.

A grand portrait gallery forming a vaulted corridor connecting two palace wings, its ceiling a continuous barrel-vault painted with a genealogical tree in fading pigments. Full-length portraits in heavy gilded frames crowd both walls from floor to cornice, many hanging at slight angles from loosened hooks. The hardwood floor is buckled where moisture has penetrated the outer wall. Carved wooden pedestals between frames bear portrait-busts in various states of damage, some missing noses or ears.

A coronation hall of extreme lateral breadth, its wide span carried not by a vault but by a flat ceiling of enormous oak beams supporting a grid of deeply carved coffers painted in faded heraldic colors. Twin colonnades of round columns line the approach to a raised marble dais supporting a canopied throne of darkened hardwood and tarnished gilt. The marble approach floor is cracked down its center, poorly repointed. Hundreds of iron coat-of-arms plaques line the walls above the colonnade.

An arcane basilica with a double-height nave divided from lower side-aisles by a clerestory of narrow stained-glass windows depicting elemental forces, their leading bent and several panes replaced with plain glass over the centuries. The nave floor is a continuous runic inscription worn by foot traffic at the center into illegibility. Free-standing iron armatures suspending crystal globes in dormant clusters hang at intervals from the vault ribs, their chains descending unevenly from hooks of different ages.

A treasure vault corridor of immense length, its groined ceiling carried on squat piers between which locked iron doors stand at regular intervals, some sealed with multiple bar-locks and wax impression-seals, others hanging ajar. The stone floor slopes almost imperceptibly toward a drain at the far end. Bracket-mounted torch-stubs and spent oil-lamps alternate along the piers. The walls between doors are scratched with inventory marks and warding symbols accumulated by successive generations of vault-keepers.

A grand ceremonial stairwell descending into a palace's lower level, its wide shallow steps of worn white marble flanked by twin rows of stone statuary on pedestals, each figure representing a mythological guardian with attributes of sword, scale, and flame. The statues nearest the bottom have been damaged and crudely repaired at various dates. The stair's ceiling is a low barrel-vault with painted coffers, several panels water-stained and peeling. Iron newel-lamps at landings burned out long ago.

A colonnaded inner courtyard open to a high stained-glass ceiling of leaded panels fitted into an iron armature, casting emerald and amber light onto cracked limestone pavers below. A central pool fed by a carved stone fish-mouth spout reflects the colored ceiling light. Colonnade capitals are densely carved with foliage motifs, the uppermost details obscured by grime. Stone benches along the colonnaded walkways are worn smooth at their seats, the backs carved with names and initials.

A vast throne hall with a barrel-vaulted ceiling ribbed in dark stone, its full length hung with double rows of dynastic banners whose lower hems are visibly moth-eaten and frayed. Flanking colonnades of octagonal pillars support the vault, their bases thickened by generations of plaster patching at the shaft-foot. The throne at the hall's terminus is elevated on seven steps of different stone, each step added by a different reign. A rose window behind the throne bleeds red light across the dais.

A multi-tier smithy hall built inside an old mine-cathedral, its tiers connected by ramps of iron grating bolted to the stone walls at angles. Each level holds forge-stations of varying age, the oldest reduced to crumbling brick with cold grates, the middle tiers still fitted with intact anvil-stands and tool-racks empty of tools. Soot blackens every surface to varying depths according to use-history. Ventilation shafts in the ceiling are partially blocked, and the heat is stale and trapped.

A great feast hall with a hammerbeam roof of aged oak, its carved angel-figures at each hammer-end darkened to near-black and several missing their outstretched wings. Long trestle tables running the hall's full length are set with tarnished pewter plate and cups as though abandoned mid-preparation. Enormous tapestries between the high windows show hunting tableaux, their lower sections faded by firelight to blank beige. Six hearths run cold, their iron fire-dogs still stacked with unlit wood.

A wizard's council chamber at the top of a tower, its circular walls lined with rotating iron bookshelves that have seized in varied positions. A central table of cracked black marble carries a three-dimensional relief-map of a continent, its ocean depths filled with blue resin now yellowed and crazing at the edges. The domed ceiling above is painted with a night sky whose gold-leaf stars have shed in patches. The floor's inlaid compass-rose is worn to a ghost at its center.

A soaring stairwell of grand ceremonial dimensions, its wide stone steps rising in a broad helix around a central void hung with a vertical cascade of iron chandeliers on a common chain. The chandeliers diminish in size with height, the lowest enormous and the topmost specks of ironwork in the upper dark. The stair's outer wall is continuous stained-glass in a heraldic narrative, lower panels intact, upper panels increasingly fragmentary and patched with lead. Carved stone handrails are worn to smooth round profiles.

A gateway hall housing five permanent portal-frames arranged in a shallow semicircle against the far wall, the frames of varying stone types representing different construction periods. The hall's vaulted ceiling has been strengthened repeatedly with iron tie-rods bolted between the ribs, giving the vault a cross-hatched appearance. The floor before each frame is stained by different-colored residue in overlapping half-circles. Heavy iron bollards on chains are anchored before each frame, and the stone between them is grooved by dragging.

A royal gallery of immense lateral span, its coffered ceiling divided into painted bays depicting an allegorical history of the realm, the earliest bays at the entrance now nearly unreadable under layers of smoke-tarnish and flaking varnish. Marble busts on alternating pilasters and freestanding pedestals line both walls, each labeled by a brass plate green with oxidation. The parquet floor, once elaborate, has been partially replaced with plain stone slabs where original sections rotted beyond repair.

A vast throne hall of kings stretching hundreds of feet from gilded portcullis to the raised dais, twin rows of age-blackened granite columns marching the full length, their capitals carved with intertwined wyrms. A threadbare crimson runner, centuries worn to bare stone at its center, leads to a towering obsidian throne framed by faded heraldic banners hanging from iron crossbeams. Coffered ceiling panels overhead hold cracked painted scenes of ancient coronations, several tiles long since fallen away.

A grand spiral stairwell climbing the interior of a wizard-tower through seventeen visible landings, each tier ringed by iron-railed balconies hung with brass lanterns burning cold amber flame. The central well drops into darkness below and opens to a distant pinhole of sky above. Carved into every baluster are weathered runes worn smooth by centuries of passing hands, and crumbling stone gargoyles perch at each landing corner, their faces chipped by age.

A dwarven forge-cathedral with twin tiers of iron-grate walkways overlooking a floor split by glowing channels of slow molten rock. Massive stone pillars reinforced with hammered iron bands rise to a soot-blackened vaulted ceiling where ancient ventilation shafts honeycomb the rock. Enormous rusted chain-hoists hang motionless above cold anvils the size of wagons, and the flagstone floor is permanently stained with a century's worth of scale, slag, and iron dust.

A war-council chamber dominated by a relief-carved stone floor depicting the entire known realm in raised topography, painted rivers and mountain ridges worn faint by decades of boots walking the map. Banner-rows of conquered and allied houses hang from ceiling beams above a heavy oak table scarred with blade-marks and ink stains. Arrow-slit windows set deep into three-foot walls throw thin afternoon light across walls covered in mounted campaign scrolls pinned with iron tacks.

A dragon's treasure vault of staggering depth, its barrel-vaulted ceiling lost in shadow above knee-deep drifts of tarnished gold coins, cracked gemstone settings, and collapsed chests spilling rotted silk. Thick square pillars march in offset rows, each base buried under accumulated hoard. Corroded iron sconces still hold stubs of ancient torches, and the stone walls are carved with territorial ward-runes half-obscured by oxidized green residue seeping from split copper ingots stacked along the vault flanks.

A vast wizard library climbing seven tiers of iron-railed balconies, each level sagging under the weight of centuries-old spellbooks. Ribbed stone vaulting spans the nave overhead, cracked where ancient binding-spells warped the mortar. Freestanding reading lecterns crowd the central floor, their wood blackened with age. Chains of dusty glass lanterns hang in long rows, and the mosaic floor beneath shows star-charts worn smooth by generations of shuffling scholars.

A great throne hall stretching two hundred paces from arched entrance to dais, its ceiling coffered in alternating panels of gilded oak and bare stone where gilt has long flaked free. Twin rows of columns march the full length, their capitals carved with interlocked serpents. Tattered royal banners hang from iron brackets, and the polished flagstone approach is worn into a visible depression by ages of petitioners walking the same central line toward the massive raised throne.

A castle inner courtyard enclosed on all four sides by colonnaded arcades, their pointed arches framing a central fountain of cracked grey marble. A stained-glass canopy of leaded panels covers the open sky overhead, casting fractured colour across the cobbled floor. Moss fills every joint between paving stones. The arcade walls are covered in bas-relief heraldic carvings worn to softness by weather and decades of rainfall filtering through the aged glazing.

A grand ceremonial stairwell rising through twelve stories of open tower interior, its wide steps of pale limestone edged in iron nosings hammered into serpentine shapes. Enormous suspended chandeliers descend on chains at every third landing, each fitted with hundreds of wax-crusted sockets. Carved stone saints and warrior figures line the stair on carved plinths, many missing hands or heads. Arrow-slit windows at each landing stripe the ascending space with thin bars of grey daylight.

A dragon's treasure vault stretching the length of a great hall, its floor buried knee-deep in gold coins, cracked gemstone settings, and collapsed crowns. Arched ceiling ribs spring from pilasters at regular intervals above, their keystones carved with territorial runes worn nearly smooth. Rusted iron torch-brackets project from the walls at head height, and heavy iron doors line the far wall, their lock-plates corroded but still holding. Coins have drifted into dunes against the pilasters.

A vast domed observatory chamber, its interior dome painted midnight blue and crowded with hand-applied gold-leaf star-positions, many flaking from the curved surface in papery curls. A huge brass armillary sphere occupies the centre of the circular mosaic floor, its rings green with verdigris. Tall arched windows ring the base of the dome, their glass ground into lenses. Shelves of logbooks and rolled charts fill every alcove carved into the thick surrounding wall.

A dwarven forge-cathedral of three descending tiers, each level opening onto the one below through arched balustrades of heat-blackened stone. Channels of molten metal run in carved stone gutters from the upper tier to huge casting-basins on the lowest floor, their surfaces glowing sulphur-orange. The vaulted ceiling above is stained centuries-dark with smoke, and enormous bellows-rigs hang from iron frames bolted into the groined arches. Hammered rune-plates are riveted across every column face from floor to capital.

A ritual spell hall with a permanent summoning-circle inlaid in copper and jet across the entire sixty-foot diameter floor. Four carved stone altars occupy the cardinal points around the circle, each bearing layered rings of hardened candle-wax centuries thick. The walls between the altars are floor-to-ceiling carved rune-panels, and a low ring of stone benches follows the room's perimeter. The ceiling above the circle rises into a lantern vault, its oculus sealed with thick purple-tinted glass.

A long banquet hall with three parallel rows of ancient oak trestle tables running its full length, their surfaces stained dark with spilled wine and scored with knife-marks. Two enormous walk-in hearths occupy the long walls midway down the hall, their stone hoods blackened from centuries of use. Tapestries depicting hunting scenes and battle maps fill every wall space between window bays, and iron chandeliers hung with beeswax tapers run the full ceiling length above the central table row.

A war-council chamber built inside a circular tower-room of considerable diameter, its floor entirely occupied by a raised relief-map table carved in stone showing a mountainous kingdom in meticulous detail. Rows of campaign banners hang from the curved walls at intervals, their fabric faded and some bearing old burn-damage. Arrow-slit windows ring the upper wall. A heavy coffered ceiling spans above, and iron sconces between the banners hold the stumps of long-burned candles pooled in hardened wax.

A portal hall of seven permanent standing-gateways arranged in a horseshoe within a vaulted chamber of dark granite. Each gateway is framed in carved stone columns with rune-inscribed lintels, the archways themselves filled with slowly churning opaque light of differing colours. The mosaic floor between the portals is inlaid with directional sigils, worn dim where travellers have shuffled repeatedly across the same lines. Chains of hanging lanterns curve between the vault ribs above, casting amber light across the darkened stone.

A magical temple basilica with a central nave flanked by side-aisles separated by double rows of rune-carved columns. Floating stone circles hang at varying heights above the nave floor, slowly rotating, covered in active glyphs that cast pale blue light across the ribbed ceiling. A great rose-window of deep violet glass dominates the apse wall. The stone floor tiles are ancient and uneven, and silver censers on tall stands occupy the aisle-corners, their contents long burned to cold ash.

A grand colonnade gallery connecting two palace wings, its vaulted ceiling running four hundred paces between entry arches. Paired columns of veined stone carry the arcade on both sides, and between every column-pair hangs a painted portrait of a past monarch or archmage, the oldest frames nearly black with age and gilt heavily chipped. The marble floor runner is worn into a shallow trough along the central walking-path. Glazed side-windows between columns admit long late-afternoon light across the stone.

A soaring spiral stairwell winding up the hollow interior of a wizard's tower, its central column carved with continuous narrative bas-relief from floor to ceiling. Iron-railinged landings project every thirty steps, each bearing a stone reading-shelf stacked with reference volumes. The stair-treads themselves are deeply hollowed at centre from long use, their edges rounded smooth. Hanging lanterns on curving iron arms project from the central column at each landing, their glass panels smoke-darkened to deep amber.

A coronation hall of immense width, its ceiling carried by four rows of clustered columns creating a five-aisled interior. The central aisle leads to a dais of three wide steps on which the ancient coronation throne sits beneath a stone canopy on carved columns. All floor surfaces are covered in large encaustic tiles of gold and crimson, many cracked through from age. Two full walls of the hall are hung with the regalia-banners of every past dynasty, overlapping in dense layered rows.

A royal portrait gallery of extraordinary length, its ceiling a continuous barrel vault painted in faded allegorical scenes. The walls between the arched window bays are panelled in dark oak, into which an unbroken sequence of monarchs' portraits has been hung in ranked rows from skirting to cornice. The oldest paintings are so darkened by varnish as to be nearly illegible. The oak floor-boards are wide and warped, and brass stanchions with velvet rope mark the central walking path.

A vast arcane basilica used for magical examinations, its nave floor marked with hundreds of individual casting-circles inlaid in polished brass, each barely large enough for a single practitioner. The ribbed stone vault is blackened unevenly where examination spells have misfired across decades. Tiered stone galleries line both side-aisles for observers. The apse end holds a massive rune-carved examination dais, and a great rose-window behind it throws coloured light across the marked floor in complex overlapping patterns.

A multi-tiered inner courtyard surrounded by three levels of arched galleries, the columns of each tier progressively more slender as they rise. The ground level centres on a large octagonal fountain of grey limestone whose carved basin overflows constantly, the water worn smooth channels into the cobbled floor over centuries. Every gallery face is hung with flowering vines now winter-bare and skeletal. The floor of each upper gallery is paved in herringbone terracotta tile, cracked and frost-heaved at intervals.

A treasure-gallery vault corridor stretching beyond sight, its barrel-vaulted ceiling interrupted at intervals by wide groin-vault bays. Locked iron-door alcoves line both walls, their frames inlaid with ward-runes long tarnished to near-invisibility. Between the doors, display plinths carry objects of every variety: sealed reliquaries, stacked coinage in glass cases, rolled maps in bronze tubes. The stone floor is dusty in the vault's furthest reaches, and wall-mounted torch-brackets have not been lit in visible generations.

A spell-research hall of cathedral proportions divided along its length by a double row of massive stone worktables permanently fixed to the floor, their surfaces scarred, stained, and carved with experimental notation from centuries of practitioners. The walls above shoulder height are covered entirely in chalkboard-finish slate, inscribed with accumulated layers of formulae never fully erased. A vaulted ceiling of fan-tracery spans above, and iron reading-cradle arms project from column faces along both sides of the central worktable rows.

A great banqueting chamber built into a cliff-face, its back wall simply the raw living rock dressed only at the columns and arches that separate it from the built hall. Three enormous hearths line the rock-face wall, and two more face them on the dressed-stone outer wall, all with deep arched hoods carved with hunting reliefs. Long oak tables fill the space in parallel rows on a herringbone-brick floor worn flat in the walking-paths. Iron chandeliers descend from a timber-beamed ceiling.

A council antechamber of great span, used for the gathering of lesser nobles before audience in the throne hall beyond. Its floor is a massive chequerboard of black and white marble, the white squares yellowed and the black squares slightly convex where centuries of feet have polished them. Arched niches around the perimeter walls hold stone busts of past lords on carved brackets. A coffered plaster ceiling spans between four corner piers, its coffers painted in alternating heraldic colours now flaking badly.

A ritual bathing-hall beneath a royal palace, its ceiling a continuous barrel vault of pale limestone running between two rows of columns whose capitals are carved with wave-scrolls. A series of sunken rectangular pools occupies the floor, their stone edges worn smooth, their bottoms green-stained. Arched niches in the side walls once held statues, most now empty or holding broken fragments. The far end of the hall rises into a domed apse inlaid with a faded mosaic sea-scene in tiny blue and gold tesserae.

A soaring gateway chamber marking the transition between the outer and inner palace precincts, its interior a single enormous room of near-cubic proportions with a ceiling vault rising eighty feet. Four permanent stone archways, one per wall, are fitted with portcullis grooves and heavy iron-banded wooden gates, three currently open. The walls between the arches carry layers of painted heraldic devices, the oldest barely visible beneath later additions. Two massive hearths flank the main entry arch, their stone surrounds carved with guardian figures in deep relief.

A dwarven hall of records beneath a mountain citadel, its ceiling carried on rows of squat but massive columns whose every surface is covered in inlaid rune-text recording clan lineages, mined seams, and battle-tallies. The floor between columns is shelved from floor to ceiling with stone-slab tablets in iron-framed racks. Narrow aisles between the racks converge on a central vaulted intersection lit by a ring of hanging iron lanterns. The tablet-edges are chipped and worn, and the oldest rack-sections lean slightly under accumulated weight.

A vast wizard's library cathedral with soaring ribbed vaults four stories overhead, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves climbing every wall, connected by iron-railed mezzanines sagging slightly with age. A rose window floods the upper tier in amber light. Rolling ladders hang askew on worn brass rails. Centuries of candle-soot blacken the coffered ceiling's carved medallions, and cracked leather spines line shelves worn smooth by ten thousand passing hands.

A throne hall of immense depth, its flagstone floor cracked down the center from some ancient tremor never repaired. Two rows of massive columns march toward a raised dais bearing an iron-and-obsidian throne flanked by moth-eaten velvet banners. Arrow-slit windows cut the thick walls at intervals, and a suspended iron chandelier — candles long cold — hangs motionless above the long royal approach, draped in old cobweb.

A castle inner courtyard enclosed by four wings of weathered stone arcade, open to the sky through a latticed iron-and-glass roof stained green with age. A fountain at center stands dry, its carved basin chipped. Cloistered walkways run the perimeter, their columns worn smooth. Moss fills every joint between flagstones, and faded heraldic shields are mounted above each arched doorway leading deeper into the fortress.

A grand spiral stairwell coiling upward through a tower for what appears to be a dozen floors. Stone steps sag at their centers from centuries of footfalls. Carved stone pilasters frame each landing, and iron sconces hold tallow candles burned to uneven stumps. Between the rail-posts, carved stone faces — each slightly different — stare inward toward the hollow center of the stair's winding eye.

A dragon's hoard vault of cathedral proportions, its barrel-vaulted ceiling lost in shadow above mountains of gold coin, tarnished silver plate, and stacked gemstones dulled by years without polish. Massive iron doors — bent outward and never fully resealed — stand at the far end. Cracked mosaic floor tiles are visible only where treasure has slid aside. Runes carved into load-bearing arches have begun to flake.

A domed observatory chamber with a vast celestial fresco wrapping the inner dome, constellations picked out in faded gilt. The floor is inlaid with a zodiac wheel in pale and dark marble, corners worn to grey smoothness. A great brass armillary sphere occupies the center, one ring broken and hanging. Arched alcoves around the perimeter hold defunct instruments on tilting tables, and cracked lenses scatter dim light across the floor.

A dwarven forge-cathedral with three tiers of working platforms descending toward a central channel of sluggish molten rock, its orange glow the only warmth in the vaulted space. Chains and pulleys criss-cross overhead, some snapped, some coiled and rusted. Massive stone bellows frames stand idle. The vaulted ceiling is entirely blackened with immovable soot, and every iron rail bears the polish of generations of gauntleted hands.

A pentagram ritual chamber with a permanent summoning circle inlaid in silver and malachite across the full breadth of the flagstone floor. Side-altars line the walls between carved pilasters, each altar surface stained dark with old wax and reagents. A coffered ceiling traces geometric divisions between painted panels now half-peeled. Tarnished silver chains hang from ceiling rings at each point of the circle, their purpose apparent and unnerving.

A long banquet hall with two rows of age-blackened oak tables stretching the full length of the room toward a cold hearth large enough to stable horses. Woven tapestries depicting ancient battles cover every stretch of wall, their colors faded and threads loose at the lower hems. A hammer-beam ceiling overhead bears carvings of intertwined beasts. Tallow-chandelier bars of wrought iron hang at intervals, candles melted to flat pools on iron plates.

A war-council chamber with a relief-map floor depicting the entire known kingdom, carved in stone and painted — though the paint is chipped across the northern ranges. A heavy oak map-table dominates the center, its surface scarred by compass-points and blade-tips over generations of planning. Rows of campaign banners hang from iron rods above the walls, and a coffered ceiling bears the names of old battles carved into each panel.

A portal hall lined on both sides with seven permanent gateway arches, their keystones carved with different rune-sets, each arch framing a shimmer of arrested transitional light. The vaulted corridor floor shows distinct worn tracks between each arch from centuries of transit. Brass plaques — several corroded past reading — are mounted beside each portal. A long ceiling of intersecting stone ribs bears hanging lanterns on chains of unequal length.

A mystical temple basilica with rune-carved walls covering every available surface from floor to vaulted crown, the oldest runes at the base nearly effaced by damp and time. Three aisles are divided by columns of dark green stone, each column's capital carved differently. The central floor bears a raised altar-platform inlaid with concentric rings of silver. Faded painted panels between the clerestory windows depict sequences of arcane ritual now difficult to read.

A grand portrait gallery connecting two fortress wings, its barrel-vaulted ceiling painted in deep blue with silver stars now dulled with age. Full-length painted portraits in heavy gilded frames — many frames cracked or missing gilding — line both walls in close-hung rows from floor to cornice. The oak floor is darkened and uneven with wear. Marble pedestals between window bays hold busts of weathered white stone, several missing features.

A coronation hall with a vast coffered ceiling of gilded compartments — most of the gold leaf gone, the exposed wood beneath dark with age. An elevated stone dais bears twin thrones of carved white marble stained amber with centuries of candle smoke. A long nave-like approach is floored in cracked pale marble. High clerestory windows of deep-dyed glass cast colored shadow-bands across the dais that shift hour by hour through the day.

A treasury vault corridor of immense length, its ceiling a succession of stone barrel vaults, each bay separated by a heavy iron portcullis — several frozen half-raised by rust. Locked iron doors of enormous thickness line both walls at intervals, their hinges corroded, their original locking mechanisms replaced multiple times evidenced by layered metalwork. The worn stone floor bears a central drainage channel, and old runes scratched into the door frames have been partially chiseled away.

A colonnaded inner court of a royal fortress, entirely enclosed beneath a stained-glass roof set in lead, many panes replaced with plain glass where colors shattered over centuries. Stone columns in four ranges define covered walkways around a central sunken garden-floor of worn flagstones. A dry stone fountain at center has been repurposed as a planter, cracked and overgrown. Carved stone bosses at column-capitals show faces eroded by long exposure to condensation.

A ceremonial staircase of immense width descending through three landings, flanked by paired stone statues on tall plinths — several statues missing heads or arms, pedestals cracked at their bases. The broad stone treads are worn concave at center. Tall arched windows on the outer wall flood each landing with grey light. A vaulted ceiling above each landing bears carved medallions, and iron torch-brackets hold the stubs of ancient torches never replaced.

A ritual spell hall with a massive inlaid floor-circle of interlocking geometric silver bands set in dark stone, spanning the entire chamber. Arched niches around the perimeter once held standing figures — most now empty, their stone bases stained where statues were dragged away. The vaulted ceiling is painted with a progression of stellar diagrams across deep blue ground, faded to near-illegibility at the far end. Old reagent stains permanently mark the altar-stone at chamber center.

A wizard's arcane basilica with a five-aisle plan, its central clerestory soaring above flanking colonnades of pale stone columns. Every arch soffit is carved with flowing runic text, the letters deep-cut and still sharp despite age. Astronomical instruments of brass and iron are mounted on brackets between columns. The floor is a complex mosaic depicting a world-map, its outer seas worn to blank grey stone by generations of footfalls near the entry.

A multi-tier inner stairwell within a mage-tower, its walls completely covered in spiraling painted sequences of spell-diagrams, floor-to-ceiling, on every course of stone. Four tiers of iron-railed landings ring the interior above. The hollow stair-shaft is criss-crossed by horizontal chains of iron hung with glass lantern-spheres, several cracked. The bottom floor is flagstone, deeply worn, and a circular glyph inlaid at the stair's base shows heavy erosion where countless feet have passed over it.

A feast hall of a mountain fortress with a ceiling of exposed hammer-beams darkened to black, hung with rusted iron chandeliers on chains, their candles pooled and dripped into stalactite formations from centuries of uninterrupted use. Three enormous hearths face each other across the room, their hearthstones cracked and iron fire-dogs corroded. Long trestle tables — scarred, stained, and repaired many times — stretch wall to wall, and faded pennants sag from the beam-ends overhead.

A throne room whose floor-to-ceiling tapestries depict an entire dynastic history across both long walls, the oldest panels near the entrance badly moth-eaten. The throne is a massive construction of dark wood and tarnished bronze, elevated on a three-step dais of cracked red marble. Arched windows with iron-framed leaded glass line the upper wall. Columns of deep-veined dark stone divide the chamber, and the carved stone floor between them bears a faded compass-rose inlaid in pale limestone.

A dragon-vault of unusual width rather than height, its ceiling a low stone barrel-vault supported on squat massive piers. The floor is covered in accumulated treasure to knee-depth across most of the chamber, with narrow paths worn clear between piers. Cracked clay tablets and rolled vellum documents are buried in drifts of coin along the walls. Carved rune-locks on the iron entry doors have been forced and never properly replaced, their mechanisms exposed and bent.

A domed celestial chamber with a painted interior dome divided into twelve stellar panels in alternating dark blue and dark green, all gilding worn to bare plaster except at the crown. The floor below is a mosaic star-chart in white and black stone, crazed with fine cracks across its surface. Eight arched alcoves hold stone reading-tables with tilted tops, their surfaces worn to silk-smoothness. A ring of iron candle-stands encircles the chamber's central unmarked stone floor-disc.

A council war-room built into a fortress's lower tier, its ceiling a shallow stone vault on corbels, its floor a continuous relief-map of the surrounding territory carved in pale limestone — mountains worn down by years of leaning study, coastal regions stained with old ink. Rows of dynastic banners hang from iron rods above the walls, some torn at the hem. A heavy round oak council-table dominates the center, its surface thick with overlaid old wax-seal impressions.

A vast wizard library stretching four tiers high, iron-railed balconies clinging to limestone walls packed with leather-bound tomes. A coffered ceiling painted with constellations peels at the gilt edges. Brass reading lamps hang on tarnished chains. The mosaic floor, worn smooth by centuries of scholar-feet, depicts a dragon coiled around an open tome. Dust motes drift through amber light from tall lancet windows.

A massive throne hall with a central dais raised on seven broad steps of black granite, flanked by twin rows of pillars carved into hooded figures. Faded battle-banners hang the full height of the walls. The iron chandelier suspended overhead holds a hundred unlit candles, wax drippings accumulated into stalactite curtains over centuries of royal ceremony.

A castle inner courtyard enclosed by four colonnaded wings, each arcade faced with weathered limestone columns. A stone fountain at the center has run green with moss, its basin cracked. Overhead, a vaulted glass-and-iron roof admits grey light, its panes streaked with decades of grime and pigeon-dust, while carved heraldic beasts watch from every column capital.

A grand spiral stairwell winding six floors up a cylindrical tower, each landing rimmed with iron balusters twisted into knotwork. Arrow-slit windows at intervals cast long diagonal light across worn stone treads. Chandeliers of antler-iron hang on chains from the vaulted apex far above, their candles guttered to stubs, wax pooled thick on every horizontal surface.

A treasure vault of cathedral proportion, the floor carpeted knee-deep in gold coins, gemstones, and tarnished plate armor. Ribbed vaulting spans the ceiling above locked iron alcoves lining each wall. Oil lanterns in iron cages illuminate columns of stacked treasure chests, their hinges rusted. Centuries of accumulated hoarding have buried the mosaic floor entirely beneath glittering, dust-dulled wealth.

A great domed observatory, the interior of its dome painted dark blue and pierced with bronze armillary rings suspended from hidden fixtures. The circular floor is inlaid with a celestial map in silver and lapis lazuli, the gilding worn away at the cardinal points by generations of standing feet. A great brass orrery occupies the chamber's center, its rings motionless.

A dwarven forge-cathedral with a soaring nave, its vaulted ceiling blackened by centuries of forge-smoke. Three great furnaces line the far wall like altars, their brick mouths cold and ash-clogged. Iron catwalks span the upper tiers where bellows-mechanisms hang rusted. Channels cut into the stone floor once ran with molten metal, now merely scorched grooves leading to cold casting pits.

A ritual summoning hall beneath a heavy ribbed vault, the stone floor engraved with a vast pentagram surrounded by concentric rings of runes worn smooth by decades of chalk-tracing. Five side-altars recessed into the walls hold iron candelabras dripping centuries of accumulated wax. The walls are hung with faded velvet panels stitched with protective sigils, their colors indistinguishable beneath soot.

A long banquet hall with trestle tables stretching the full length of a barrel-vaulted room, their oak surfaces scarred and wine-stained from generations of feasting. Six enormous hearths line one wall, their stone surrounds carved with hunting scenes worn soft by centuries of heat and scrubbing. Rows of tattered tapestries depicting dynastic histories hang between iron torch-brackets above the diners' benches.

A war-council chamber dominated by a vast relief-map table of carved stone, mountain ranges and river-valleys rendered in painstaking detail, the painted colors faded to ghosts. Battle-standard rows hang from ceiling brackets along both walls, the oldest reduced to thread-bare rags on their poles. Arched windows overlook a killing-ground below, their stone sills gouged by generations of gauntleted hands gripping them.

A portal hall of immense width, seven permanent archways of different-colored stone arranged in a curved colonnade. Each arch frames a slow-churning veil of light marking a distant destination. The marble floor between them is worn into hollows at each threshold by centuries of arriving and departing feet. Carved inscription panels above each arch have been re-chiseled multiple times, old letters still faintly legible.

A magical temple-basilica with walls carved floor-to-ceiling in dense rune-panels, each symbol underlit by faint bioluminescent lichen that has colonized the incised channels over centuries. Double rows of columns support a coffered ceiling where iron prayer-circles hang at staggered heights. The nave floor is a single continuous mosaic of a stylized sun, its tesserae cracked and re-grouted in mismatched colors.

A grand portrait gallery occupying a vaulted corridor of immense length, gilt-framed canvases hung three rows high on both walls from floor to the springing of the arch. The faces of five centuries of rulers stare outward, the oldest portraits cracked and yellowed behind dusty glass. A threadbare carpet runner traces the full length of the stone floor, its pattern obliterated at the center.

A coronation hall with a polished obsidian floor reflecting the stained-glass rose window set into the far wall above the throne platform. Pairs of enormous pillars march toward the dais, their carved capitals depicting crowning ceremonies. The vaulted ceiling bears painted heraldry in gilt and crimson, large sections flaked away to bare plaster. Crown-shaped chandeliers hang between each bay, heavy with melted taper-wax.

A multi-tier ceremonial stairwell with a wide central flight flanked by twin ascending returns, all three tiers lined with marble statuary of past arch-mages on tall plinths. The coffered ceiling far above is barely visible through layers of hanging iron chandeliers descending on chains of differing lengths. The stone balustrade is cracked at intervals, repairs visible in mismatched stone plugged with aging mortar.

A vault-corridor of enormous width, its barrel vault supported by ribs of dressed stone, the walls lined on both sides with locked iron doors set into arched recesses. Every door bears a different wax seal layered over older seals, decades of administrative color-coding. The stone floor between the rows is grooved by the iron wheels of heavy strongbox trolleys, the ruts worn inches deep.

A sprawling arcane basilica with a nave broad enough to stage a cavalry drill, its clerestory windows of amber glass casting the full length of the floor in honey-colored light. Towering iron bookcases have been dragged between the columns over centuries, converting a ceremonial hall into an improvised repository. Scrolls and folios overflow every shelf, stacked in towers against the pillar bases.

A great cloistered garden courtyard enclosed by four wings of pointed arches, the colonnade walkways paved in worn limestone slabs. At the center, a dry fountain basin has been colonized by decades of moss and self-seeded herbs. The inner faces of the arches still show painted decoration, the colors bleached to pale suggestion by generations of weather filtering through the open crown above.

A royal arcane chamber built as a tall octagonal room, each of the eight walls bearing a full-height tapestry depicting an elemental domain. A raised central platform of polished serpentine holds the throne of carved ebony, its canopy of iron spires hung with faded silk. The ribbed dome above is painted with a celestial map whose gilded stars are peeling in wide flakes.

A dwarven multi-tier smithy hall descending three levels below the surface, visible from a wide upper gallery behind iron railings. Each lower level holds a row of abandoned anvils, their surfaces pocked by generations of hammer-blows. Cooling channels of cut stone run between each station toward a central drainage cistern. The arched ceiling is thick with ancient soot, and every iron fixture is furred in rust.

A vast antechamber preceding the inner sanctum, square in plan and roofed with a shallow sail vault decorated in faded fresco. Rows of waiting-benches in dark oak line three walls, their surfaces polished smooth by centuries of anxious hands. Trophy weapons are mounted above each bench in declining order of age, the oldest blades reduced to rust-silhouettes on their iron mounting brackets.

A spell-circle hall with a mosaic floor dominated by a fifty-foot ritual diagram inlaid in silver and jet, its geometric arms extending to the base of the encircling columns. Between each column, a shallow niche holds an iron stand sized for a spell-component chest, most stands empty and corroded. The groin-vaulted ceiling above the circle is scorched in a radial pattern from some ancient working.

A feast hall of generous proportion with a hammerbeam roof of smoke-darkened oak spanning the full width, the carved wooden angels at each hammer-end missing faces and hands. Long trestle tables fill the floor in six parallel rows, their boards gouged and stained. Six enormous fireplaces alternate down each long wall, their stone overmantels carved with boar-hunt scenes, the hearths cold and ash-heaped.

A treasury gallery laid out as a wide vaulted hall with display plinths arranged in formal rows, each originally bearing a magical artifact. Most plinths stand empty, their velvet surfaces faded into pale rectangles where objects once rested. Iron display cabinets line the side walls, their glass fronts cracked or replaced with warped wood panels. The barrel-vaulted ceiling retains its painted inventory inscriptions, though many are crossed out.

A grand colonnade walkway connecting two palace wings, its double row of columns supporting a continuous barrel vault. Clerestory windows between each column bay are glazed in alternating green and gold, the leading cracked in many panes. Between columns, bronze portrait busts on tall plinths represent centuries of court officials, many nameplates missing or corroded to illegibility, the stone plinths stained dark at their bases.

A vast wizard's library cathedral, soaring ribbed vaults lost in shadow above tier upon tier of oak galleries, spiral iron staircases connecting each level, ten thousand grimoires packed into age-darkened shelves. Brass reading-lamp brackets line every colonnade. The flagstone floor is grooved by centuries of scholarly foot-traffic, and cracked leather spines shed dust into amber pools of candlelight.

A great throne hall stretching three hundred paces from iron-banded doors to the raised dais, the central throne carved from a single block of obsidian veined with silver. Rows of ancestral banners hang from iron rods along both walls, threadbare at their lower hems. A mosaic floor depicting a founding war runs the full length of the approach, its colored tiles worn smooth by millennia of petitioners.

A castle inner courtyard enclosed by four wings of arched colonnades, a moss-ringed fountain at the center whose carved basin lip has sunk unevenly into the cobblestones over long centuries. An enormous stained-glass roof of iron-framed panes covers the court, throwing diamond lozenges of color across the worn stone pavings below. Potted topiary shaped into heraldic beasts line the arcade's inner face.

A grand ceremonial stairwell winding upward inside a hollow tower, wide enough for eight abreast, each landing flanked by life-sized knight statues on plinths. Chains of iron chandeliers hang at every quarter-turn, their candles burned to stubs of tallow. The balustrade is carved continuous stone, its handrail polished bright by ten generations of passing hands while the carved frieze below it has softened with age.

A dragon's treasure vault of cathedral proportions, its barrel-vaulted ceiling resting on thick pillars whose bases vanish beneath a sea of loose coin, tarnished plate, and gem-encrusted relics. Iron-banded lock-doors line the side walls at intervals, each sealed with wax stamps long since cracked. A single heavy iron chandelier sags overhead, half its brackets empty, the remaining candles guttered to black stubs.

An observatory dome of immense span, its interior ceiling painted in deep blue and mapped with silver-leaf constellations, each star-point capped with a faceted crystal lens. A spiral walkway of wrought-iron circles the inner circumference at mid-height, connecting swiveling brass instrument platforms. The stone floor below is engraved with a great celestial chart, its compass-lines worn faint by repeated measurement and scholarly pacing over centuries.

A dwarven forge-cathedral of multi-tier construction, hammer galleries rising on both sides above a central channel of orange-glowing molten metal that runs the length of the hall in a stone-cut trough. Exhaust shafts pierce the vaulted ceiling at regular intervals, their stone lips blackened by endless smoke. The anvil platforms are scarred and dented, every iron pillar support bearing the dents of generations of stray hammer blows.

A ritual summoning hall with a vast permanent pentagram inlaid in silver and iron into the stone floor, surrounded by concentric inscription rings in a dozen archaic scripts. Eight side-altars occupy arched recesses along the curved walls, their candle-crowned surfaces thick with dripped wax. The coffered ceiling above is carved with warding symbols, many of them deliberately defaced and recarved as doctrines changed across the centuries.

A long banquet hall with two parallel rows of trestle tables running its full length, their oak surfaces stained dark by countless feasts. Three enormous walk-in hearths occupy each long wall, their stone mantels carved with hunting scenes now soot-blurred. Moth-eaten tapestries hang between the hearths, depicting dynastic celebrations, and iron chandeliers bristling with candles are lowered by rope-and-pulley from the hammer-beam ceiling above.

A war-council chamber dominated by a sand-table relief map of an entire kingdom, set in a massive frame of carved oak at the room's center. Banner-rows of every vassal house hang along the stone walls, several reduced to hanging fragments. A gallery tier runs the perimeter at head height, accessible by short flights of stone stair, giving commanders an elevated view of the strategic table below.

A portal hall with seven permanent gateway arches standing in a curved row, each framing a different shimmering threshold sealed behind iron-grate doors of extraordinary thickness. The stone floor between them is scored by decades of heavy cart traffic hauling goods between destinations. Carved name-tablets above each arch have been chiseled and re-chiseled as allegiances changed, leaving palimpsests of old destinations visible beneath the current inscriptions.

A magical basilica with a wide central nave flanked by colonnaded aisles, floating geometric sigil-rings turning slowly at different heights beneath the vaulted ceiling. The rune-carved walls are dense with layered inscription work, older scripts peeking beneath newer additions where stone has been re-smoothed and reused. Mosaic panels between column bays show the founding of the order, their tesserae cracked and re-grouted in mismatched colors.

A grand portrait gallery corridor connecting two palace wings, its vaulted ceiling resting on engaged columns between which full-length royal portraits hang in gilded frames darkened with age-varnish. The stone floor runner is worn to a deep central groove. Occasional marble busts on narrow plinths punctuate the colonnade rhythm, several with chipped noses and re-set bronze eyes that replaced originals lost in some long-ago upheaval.

A coronation hall of immense breadth, its ceiling a grid of heavy stone coffers painted with heraldic devices now faded to ghost-colors. A long central aisle leads between ranked carved pews to a raised double-throne on a stepped dais, the throne canopy of iron and ancient velvet. Tall lancet windows march along both walls, their leaded stained-glass narrative panels depicting the dynasty's founding in colors that have deepened over centuries.

A cloistered inner courtyard of four colonnaded walks, each walk a deep arcade of rounded arches resting on paired columns with carved capitals. At the center a stone well-head surrounded by cracked paving slabs where frost-heave has buckled the ground over long winters. Carved stone tracery fills the spandrels of every arch, its fine detail softened to gentle blurs by weathering across uncountable seasons of rain and ice.

A wizard's arcane basilica with three aisles separated by tall columns, their capitals carved as interlocking serpents. Enchanted glass spheres hang at varying heights between the columns, giving off a cold persistent luminescence that throws no shadows. Carved scroll-brackets project from the upper walls bearing stacked instrument cases and rolled parchment tubes, accumulated over generations of researchers, their wooden cases warped and their leather ties cracked with age.

A vault-corridor of imposing length, its groined ceiling resting on thick piers between which iron lock-doors of enormous weight are set flush with the stone. Brass plaques beside each door record inventories in cramped archaic script, many plaques polished blank by later re-use. The stone floor bears the deep parallel grooves of metal-shod chest-runners, worn by centuries of treasury deliveries into the dark interior.

A ceremonial antechamber preceding a great keep's inner sanctum, its domed ceiling decorated with a plaster relief of interlocking knotwork now partially collapsed in one quadrant, the gap exposing bare rubble-fill above. Four enormous hearths occupy the corners, their iron fire-dogs shaped as heraldic beasts, and the walls carry full-height carved wainscoting of age-blackened oak inlaid with tarnished silver heraldic devices.

A spiral stairwell of extraordinary height inside a wizard's tower, the open stone well at its center dropping and rising many floors. Iron-bracket torcheries spiral upward in alignment with the steps. Every dozen courses the stone wall is interrupted by an arched landing-window overlooking inner-castle roofscapes, its stone sill worn concave by countless observers who rested there across the tower's long history, watching events unfold below.

A vast dwarven throne hall carved entirely from living rock, its ceiling a fan-vault of extraordinary complexity chiseled from the mountain's native stone. Rows of basalt columns support side galleries packed with carved ancestor-busts. The floor is a polished expanse of layered marble inlay depicting underground kingdoms, its surface worn glass-smooth at the central processional lane while geometric margins retain their original fine-cut crispness.

A spell-hall with a high circular floor-plan, its single vast summoning circle laid in contrasting stone inlay occupying almost the entire chamber floor. Curved walls carry carved rune-columns from floor to ceiling, their inscription work so dense the stone between characters is barely visible. Overhead a coffered dome rises, its coffers each carved with a different binding-glyph, the outermost ring of coffers broken open in places by some long-ago magical catastrophe.

A great hall of kings with hammer-beam roof of dark oak, each beam-end carved as a heraldic beast. Two long hearths run along one wall beneath a continuous stone mantel shelf bearing trophy armor and ancestral helms tarnished to dull gray. The opposing wall is covered floor-to-ceiling with layered battle tapestries, the lowest course partially obscured where later banners have been hung over them to signal new allegiances.

A colonnaded treasury wing of palace scale, its wide central passage flanked by deep arched alcoves each sealed with iron grilles behind which display-cases of carved stone hold royal regalia. The vaulted ceiling above the passage bears painted coffers, their painted surfaces cracked and yellowed. The floor is a geometric mosaic of white and black stone, its pattern continuous but interrupted by later repair-patches of mismatched tile where heavier loads cracked the original work.

A ritual antechamber preceding an inner sanctum, its four walls entirely covered in carved stone bas-relief panels depicting a mythological cycle, the earliest panels at low height worn nearly featureless by centuries of worshippers pressing hands against them in reverence. A ring of iron candelabra of standing height surround the central preparation-slab of polished granite, each candelabra arm fitted with melted-wax stubs and fresh replacements in no particular order.

A multi-tier inner courtyard open to the sky but fully enclosed by palace wings on all four sides, each wing presenting three stacked floors of arched colonnades overlooking the space. Stone stairs connect the colonnade tiers at each corner, their balustrades carved in continuous scroll-work. The courtyard floor is a deteriorating geometric pavement around a central octagonal fountain pool, its carved rim cracked along one face and re-mortared in a visible thick bead of gray.

A vast wizard library occupying a cathedral-vaulted nave, shelves rising seven stories behind iron balcony rails bolted into crumbling mortar. Coffered stone ceilings drip centuries of candle-tallow across carved boss-roses. A cracked rose-window spills amber light onto mosaic floors worn smooth by generations of shuffling feet. Rolling ladders hang tilted on their rails, and collapsed stacks lean against reading lecterns black with age.

A throne hall of immense width, its central throne raised on nine broad steps of age-pitted granite, approached by a floor of cracked marble inlaid with a tarnished kingdom's coat of arms. Rows of iron-banded oak banners hang from corbelled brackets fifty feet overhead. Stained-glass lancets line both flanks, their lead-lines sagging, casting pools of colored light onto a worn runner of faded crimson cloth.

A castle inner courtyard enclosed by four-story colonnaded galleries, their arched walkways latticed with decades of creeping stone-moss. A central fountain of carved seahorses stands half-drained, its basin ringed with old coin-offerings tarnished green. An overhead grid of wrought-iron glazing frames a stained-glass roof of sky-blue panels, several replaced with plain glass after old storm damage, the mismatch adding a lived-in honesty.

A grand spiral stairwell ascending a drum tower of pale ashlar, the stone steps worn concave at each center-tread by uncounted boots across centuries. Hanging chandeliers of forged iron descend on chains at staggered heights, their candles burned to stumps. Statues of armored lords occupy niches at every landing, shields chipped and noses broken, garland-draped in moth-eaten ceremonial ribbon that has never been replaced.

A dragon's treasure vault of overwhelming horizontal sprawl, its barrel-vaulted ceiling lost in shadow far above a floor buried under coin-drifts knee-deep in places. Heaped plate-armor, collapsed gem-chests, and tarnished crowns pile against groined walls fitted with iron torch-brackets long since gone cold. A wide central aisle has been worn bare by something immense moving through regularly, the coins pushed aside in two long, parallel ridges.

A domed observatory chamber of tremendous girth, its inner dome surface painted with a celestial map now flaking at the edges where plaster has separated from stone. Inlaid floor-brass traces an orrery diagram across aged marble worn smooth at the observation points. Narrow arch-windows pierce the drum at regular intervals, and a massive central armillary sphere of tarnished bronze sits on a cracked stone pedestal, rings slightly misaligned.

A dwarven forge-cathedral with a nave of blackened granite piers rising to a smoke-stained barrel vault, its keystone carved with a hammer-and-flame emblem worn near-flat. Twin channels of cooling slag run the hall's length flanking a broad central floor of heat-cracked flagstones. Tiered forge-platforms climb the side walls, accessed by iron catwalks bolted into the rock, their railings wrapped with decades of singed leather grip-cloth.

A ritual chamber of octagonal plan, its floor entirely consumed by an immense pentagram inlaid in tarnished silver, the lines worn and re-incised so many times the grooves are deep and irregular. Candle-altars occupy all eight wall-recesses, wax accumulated over generations into baroque formations rising two feet from their stone shelves. A coffered vault overhead bears painted runes in concentric rings, the outermost layer faded to near-invisibility with age.

A banquet hall of extraordinary length, parallel trestle tables of scarred oak stretching from the screens-passage to the high-table dais without interruption. Two massive walk-in hearths bracket the long walls, their mantels blackened by centuries of roaring fires. Above, hammerbeam trusses carry iron chandelier-rings dense with candle-stubs, and faded hunting tapestries fill every panel between the high windows, their bottom hems worn ragged where they brush the flagstones.

A war-council chamber of solid proportions, its central floor dominated by a raised relief-map of an entire kingdom rendered in painted stone, the mountain pigment worn pale at the ranges most frequently discussed. Banner-rows of conquered territories hang from horizontal lances along all walls, many banners duplicated where the originals rotted and were replaced. Candle-stubs crowd the map's borders and a ring of heavy oak chairs surrounds it, legs uneven on worn stone.

A portal hall of cathedral-corridor proportions, seven permanent gateway-arches lining each side wall at measured intervals, their frames carved from different colored stone suggesting different origins. Worn bronze plaques below each arch bear destination-names in lettering rubbed nearly smooth. The flagstone floor between the portals shows clear paths of heavier wear directly before each arch, and the vault above is dark with the accumulated soot of uncountable activation-flares across many centuries.

A mystical temple basilica of soaring height, its nave flanked by columns carved with continuous bands of protective runes re-incised so many generations deep that some letters have become abstract grooves. The apse holds a floating ritual-circle of dim amber light, suspended without visible support, its outer ring slightly wobbled as if an anchoring stone beneath the floor has subsided over centuries. Dusty votive offerings crowd every surface of the side-altars.

A portrait gallery of immense vaulted length, gilt frames ranked in floor-to-ceiling double rows along both walls with intervening arched windows flooding the pale stone floor with afternoon light. Centuries of subjects stare from darkened canvases, lower portraits occasionally veiled by velvet where paint has crumbled. Carved pedestals bearing marble busts of monarchs occupy the window-bays, several busts now missing noses or crowns, losses never repaired.

A coronation hall of towering vaulted grandeur, its ribbed ceiling rising to a central crown-boss far overhead, the painted gold leaf of the boss now tarnished and flaking. A wide approach of cracked marble tiles runs from the west door to the stepped dais, bordered by enormous column-shafts of mottled granite. Along both flanks, clerestory windows of thick stained-glass cast wavering bands of colored light that shift across the floor as clouds move outside.

A soaring ceremonial staircase of double-return design, its twin stone flights ascending from a broad landing of veined marble to a gallery level above. Carved balustrades of limestone bear centuries of accumulated touch-polish on every newel-cap, worn smooth and ivory-bright. Between the two ascending flights, a niche occupies the entire landing-wall, holding a cracked mosaic map of the old empire, several tesserae replaced in mismatched colors where the original stones were lost.

A cloistered inner courtyard open to weather beneath a pane of enchanted glass set in iron tracery far overhead, its four surrounding galleries of pointed arches casting latticed shade across a central herb-garden run wild with decades of untended growth. Each arch-spandrel bears carved medallions slowly being consumed by green lichen, and a low-walled fountain at the garden's center has been colonized by moss until its carved rim is entirely softened.

A royal arcane chamber of square plan and great height, its four walls covered floor-to-vault in interlocking rectilinear shelving housing crystal orbs of varying size, the lower shelves accessible and frequently dusted, the upper shelves clearly untouched for lifetimes. A coffered ceiling of dark oak shows old water staining in one corner, the wood swollen and the pattern distorted. A wide working table of scarred stone sits at center, its surface covered in dried wax and ink-stains.

A summoning hall with a smooth circular floor dominated by a vast inlaid circle of pale stone set against dark, its inner geometric divisions precise but worn at several nodes where feet have scuffed repeatedly across them during long rituals. The surrounding walls bear four massive arch-alcoves at the cardinal points, each fitted with wrought-iron candle-brackets crusted in generations of wax overflow. Ribbed vaulting overhead carries the weight of the tower above, its keystones carved with containment-wards.

A vault-corridor of long barrel-vaulted extension, iron-banded doors lining both walls at intervals of twenty feet, each fitted with multiple lock-plates of different ages and styles added over centuries as security fashions changed. The corridor floor is worn in a single central strip of extraordinary smoothness while the flanking stone remains rough. Wall-mounted torch-brackets alternate with plaque-niches holding small carved warnings in an archaic script now partially indecipherable to any living reader.

A great feast-room of generous width, its hammerbeam ceiling painted in alternating chevron panels of red and gold now substantially faded and spotted with old smoke-staining. A single enormous hearth dominates the head wall, its lintel carved with a boar-hunt in high relief, the stone abraded by centuries of hands reaching to steady themselves on the mantel-shelf. Long side-walls carry continuous tapestry depicting a dynastic genealogy stitched in wool now partially moth-eaten in the upper sections.

A wizard library of multi-tier design within a converted chapter-house space, its original groined vaulting now partly obscured by intermediate floors of iron grating inserted at two heights to gain additional shelf-space. The grating-floors sag visibly toward their centers under the weight of accumulated volumes. Brass reading-chains dangle from every shelf-edge on the upper levels, tarnished green, and the ambient smell of old parchment and cold stone is pervasive even in the description's silence.

A multi-tier stairwell ascending a full castle keep, its central shaft open from ground level to a glazed lantern dome at the top, afternoon light filtering down in a single wide column past six levels of encircling gallery-balconies. Each balcony rail shows different stone-carving styles accumulating across centuries of repair. The lowest landing's mosaic floor is well-preserved; at each higher level, more tesserae are missing and infilled with plain stone, marking decades of declining maintenance as priorities shifted.

A treasure gallery of cathedral proportions with arched side-aisles flanking a wider central nave, display plinths of carved stone holding objects of varying antiquity beneath dusty glass cases of iron and crystal. The ceiling bosses above each plinth carry carved emblems corresponding to the object below, a curatorial system old enough that some correspondences have become unclear. The mosaic floor between display-rows shows heavy wear at the start of each aisle and lighter wear toward the far ends.

A domed arcane basilica of tremendous interior volume, its dome carried on eight massive piers of dark stone connected by pointed arches, the spandrels filled with mosaic constellations slowly losing individual tiles to the pull of centuries. Floating ritual-circles of pale blue luminescence drift at mid-height, slightly out of round as their anchoring enchantments age. The wide floor below shows a faint geometric diagram incised into the stone, partially obscured by accumulated ritual-wax and powdered chalk.

A map-chamber and strategic war-room of generous square plan, its floor covered entirely by an inlaid stone relief-map of a mountain kingdom, the paint renewed so many generations over the same base-carving that colors have built up in subtle ridges. Heavy oak war-tables crowd the map's border, their surfaces covered with scored measurement-marks, carved tallies, and old ink-stains. Four banner-rows of regimental standards hang from lateral beams, the oldest banners reduced to fringe and fragment.

A throne hall of colossal proportion, its vaulted ceiling lost in shadow above twin rows of centuries-worn columns draped in faded war-banners. The central dais rises on seven broad steps of cracked marble, the throne itself carved from a single obsidian slab. Torch-brackets of tarnished bronze line every pillar, and the mosaic floor—kings and dragons interlocked—is ground smooth by ten thousand years of court procession.

A grand spiral stairwell ascending the interior of a wizard-tower, each landing framed by lancet windows of amber glass throwing warm angular light across worn stone treads. Iron chandeliers hang on chains of unequal length, their candles long spent and replaced and spent again. Carved runes spiral up the central newel post, the oldest worn to near-illegibility, the newest merely centuries old. Gargoyle corbels support each landing.

A vast dwarven forge-cathedral, its nave spanned by a coffered ceiling of soot-blackened granite above three great sunken channels of glowing molten rock. Ranked anvil-stations occupy the floor like pews, their surfaces pocked and starred from aeons of use. Chain-hoists hang from iron rails bolted to the ceiling vaults. Enormous double-bellows flank the master forge at the apse, their leather cracked and patched a dozen times over.

A war-council chamber deep within a fortress keep, its walls covered floor to ceiling with tactical relief-maps carved in limestone and inlaid with colored stone. A central table of age-blackened oak bears a raised terrain model of the surrounding kingdom, pins of tarnished silver still marking positions from a campaign long concluded. Rows of ranked banners descend from ceiling mounts above, their heraldry faded to suggestion.

A treasure vault corridor of staggering length, arched in ribbed stone with a vaulted ceiling bearing painted heraldry obscured by centuries of dust. Iron-banded doors line both walls at measured intervals, each sealed with wax-stamp and lock. Between the doors, niches hold bronze busts of former treasurers. The floor is worn deep at the center by centuries of cart-traffic, and the stone smells of old metal and dry parchment.

A banquet hall of royal scale, its ceiling supported by a double colonnade of pale stone columns from which suspended chandeliers descend on iron chains. Long trestle tables of ancient oak run the hall's full length, their surfaces carved with initials and old spills worn glass-smooth. At the far end a vast hearth of carved stone bears the arms of a dynasty above its mantel, the fireback black with centuries of use.

A ritual chamber of octagonal plan, its floor inlaid with an elaborate summoning-circle of silver and jet in concentric bands. Eight side-altars occupy each wall-face, their surfaces cluttered with centuries of accumulated wax-drip, ash, and spent rune-chalk. A domed ceiling above is painted with the night sky as seen on a specific forgotten date, the constellation-lines cracking with age. Stone channels in the floor carry residual energy toward the circle's center.

A cloistered inner courtyard enclosed within castle walls, its perimeter formed by a low colonnade of weathered arches supporting a narrow stone walkway above. At the center a fountain basin of green-stained marble still issues water through a carved lion-mouth worn featureless by centuries of flow. Flagstones below are cracked and lifted by old roots, the joints filled with moss. Stained-glass panels close the courtyard roof above the central open well.

A wizard's library of cathedral scale, its shelves rising six galleries high behind wrought-iron balcony rails bolted to columns of pale limestone. Rolling ladders on brass rails serve each tier, their wood worn at the grip-points to a bright polish. The ceiling is coffered and painted with an astronomical chart. Freestanding reading desks of ancient oak occupy the nave floor, their surfaces tilted and leather-padded, the leather split and repaired many times over.

A portal hall of soaring rectangular proportion, its long axis lined with nine permanent arched portals framed in carved stone, their interior fields shimmering with residual light of varying hues. The vaulted ceiling above is inscribed with navigational runes in layered scripts, the oldest in a language no longer spoken. Worn stone paths lead from each portal to a central hub-roundel of mosaic, its pattern recording destination-symbolism in faded tile.

A coronation hall of immense width, its span crossed by three great transverse arches supporting a ceiling of gilded coffering now tarnished to dull ochre. The approach corridor is floored in alternating black and cream stone, worn convex at the crown by generations of ceremonial procession. Enormous rose windows at each gable end flood the interior with colored light, their leading ancient and bowed. Carved stone monarchs line the side-wall niches, each bearing a different crown.

A grand observatory dome, its hemispherical ceiling of pale stone perforated by a ring of narrow windows and a central oculus. The interior floor is inlaid with a celestial map in brass and lapis, the brass worn bright at the walking-paths. A rotating armillary of enormous scale hangs centrally on chains, its rings of tarnished bronze inscribed with angular runes. Stepped viewing galleries rise around the perimeter on iron-railed platforms of weathered timber.

A vaulted corridor gallery spanning a full wing, its length broken by arched bays each containing a framed portrait of an ancient ruler or archmage. The ribbed ceiling above is painted with lozenges of faded color. A continuous stone bench runs the full length of each wall below the portraits, its surface worn smooth and hollowed. Tall arrow-slit windows punctuate the exterior wall, their stone embrasures deeply worn and their glass replaced with plain quarries of old vintage.

A summoning hall of rectangular plan, its ceiling rising to a pointed barrel vault of bare grey limestone. The floor bears a permanent inlaid pentagram of contrasting stone, its arms terminating in rune-carved medallions. Five stone plinths at the points support bronze braziers of considerable age, their interiors fire-blackened and their feet stained with centuries of poured offering. The walls bear relief-carved panels depicting ancient compacts, their figures worn smooth at the outstretched hands.

A great stair of ceremonial width descending through three open tiers, its carved stone balustrades bearing heraldic animals at each newel worn soft by hands. Pairs of standing stone warriors flank each landing, their faces abraded. Rows of iron chandeliers descend through the open center of the stairwell on chains of varying lengths, hung with clustering candle-spurs. The treads are each worn in a broad concave curve at center, deepest at the lowest flight.

A royal treasure gallery of vaulted plan, its floor covered knee-deep in accumulated coin and artifact in the older reaches, the accumulation thinning toward the guarded entrance. Coffered bays above are painted with inventories in an archaic hand, many superseded and annotated over. Iron torch-stands rise from the coin-floor at intervals, their bases lost below the surface. The walls display mounted weapons, crowns in locked cases of yellowed glass, and chests of iron-banded oak standing open and overfull.

A great arcane basilica, its nave roofed by a pointed vault painted with a cosmological diagram in fading ochre and blue. Side aisles are separated from the nave by a colonnade of slender clustered columns, each base worn to rough irregularity. Stained-glass windows in the clerestory above are ancient beyond dating, their leading sagged and some panels replaced with plain glass that breaks the scene. Stone lecterns in the nave hold great open books chained to their desks.

A castle inner courtyard of vast enclosure, its four walls of dressed stone rising four stories above an open sky. Colonnaded arcades line each ground-floor wall behind pointed arches worn round at their edges.
