A central pool of still grey water reflects the arcade above, its stone lip cracked and patched with old mortar. Carved drain-spouts project from the upper walls, their carved animal-heads green with centuries of water-stain. Iron lamp-brackets on each pillar are dark with age.

A war-room of fortress scale, its vaulted ceiling hung with ranked battle-standards of past campaigns in varying states of preservation, the oldest reduced to fringe and thread. A central stone table bears a relief-map of the realm carved into its upper surface, worn and repaired over centuries with differing stones filling old damage. Ranked chairs of age-darkened oak surround it. Sealed map-chests line the walls between torch brackets, each bound with iron and labeled in fading script.

A feast hall of lateral grandeur, its width greater than its height and its ceiling formed by a low vault of ribbed stone supported on two inner rows of heavy round columns. Trestle tables crowd the floor in long ranks, their surfaces carved and stained by generations. Three enormous hearths occupy one long wall, their carved stone surrounds blackened above the lintel, their fireback-plates corroded dark. Tapestried scenes of hunting and harvest hang the opposite wall, faded and patched.

A multi-tiered smithy hall of dwarven construction, its nave rising past four galleries of workshop-balconies each serving a different forging specialty. The vaulted ceiling is supported on columns of rough-cut granite braced with iron strapping added at different periods. Cooling racks of wrought iron descend from the ceiling on chains. The stone floor is deeply scored and pocked with dropped scale and gravel, the original dressed surface visible only at the margins near the walls.

A ritual spell-hall of elongated octagonal plan, its stone walls carved floor to ceiling with layered rune-scripts in at least four successive periods and styles, each generation having inscribed over and between the older work. The floor bears a complex working-circle inlaid in contrasting stone and metal, showing evidence of repair and re-inscription. A domed ceiling above is painted with constellation-maps in fading mineral pigment, and eight iron brazier-stands ring the perimeter.

A grand colonnade walk connecting two fortress wings, its outer arcade of pointed arches framing views into a walled secondary courtyard below. The inner wall carries a continuous painted frieze of historical narrative, its colors cracked and lightened with age, portions over-painted in a later style. The stone floor is worn in two parallel paths of deep concavity following the heaviest traffic-lines. Pendant lanterns on iron chains hang between each arch-springer above, their glass clouded.

A magical temple-basilica of wide nave and low triforium, its walls carved entirely in interlocking rune-registers that glow with a faint residual light beneath centuries of accumulated candle-smoke. The apse at the far end rises behind a carved stone iconostasis of considerable age, its central arch framing a suspended circle of pale arcane light. Mosaic floors in geometric pattern cover the nave, their tile surface worn concave at the threshold and before the altar-steps.

A great antechamber of soaring rectangular proportion, its ceiling a fan-vault of intricate stone tracery meeting at a central pendant boss of carved arms. The floor is a chequerwork of black and pale stone worn deeply convex at the threshold and the axial path. Niches in the long side walls hold full-scale stone effigies of former lords with painted faces now faded to ghost-traces. A double-stair at the far end rises to flanking arched doorways of panelled oak, their surfaces dark with centuries of handling.

A vast wizard library ascending seven gallery tiers, iron-railed balconies stacked beneath a coffered stone ceiling dark with centuries of candle-smoke. Thousands of shelved grimoires lean at worn angles, their spines faded. A cracked mosaic floor maps constellations underfoot, tesserae missing in places. Brass reading-chains dangle from wheeled ladders. Guttered wax has pooled into thick pale rivers along every shelf edge.

A throne hall of enormous breadth, its vaulted ceiling lost in shadow above rows of smoke-darkened stone pillars. A long approach of cracked marble leads to a raised dais bearing a single massive iron throne, its arms worn bright by countless hands. Faded dynastic banners hang the full height of the walls, their embroidered heraldry softened by generations of dust.

A castle inner courtyard enclosed on all four sides by tiered colonnaded arcades, their carved arches weathered to softness. At the center a broad octagonal fountain pools dark water beneath a stained-glass ceiling that fractures amber and blue across the flagstones below. Moss has crept between every joint. Crumbling stone planters line the lower arcade, their soil long gone dry.

A grand spiral stairwell climbing the interior of a tower without end visible above, each landing cantilevered from the curved wall with no central column. Rusted iron chandeliers hang at irregular intervals on chains of different lengths. The stone steps are bowed deeply at their centers, worn hollow by ages of traffic. Carved faces watch from every corbel, their features smoothed to near-blankness.

A dragon vault of crushing scale, its low barrel-vaulted ceiling pressing close over a floor submerged knee-deep in tarnished gold coin, cracked gemstones, and bent crown-metal. Iron vault-doors line the far walls, hinges fused with age-rust. Torch-brackets hold only cold stubs. The accumulated weight of metal has fractured the floor slabs beneath, tilting whole sections at slow angles over decades.

A domed observatory chamber with a vast hemispherical ceiling painted in deep indigo, scored with gilded constellation-lines that have flaked at their edges. The circular floor inlaid in white marble shows the full celestial sphere mapped in obsidian. Tall arched windows ring the drum below the dome, their glass thick and bubbled with age. A central orrery-mount of bronze rises empty from the floor.

A dwarven forge-cathedral of immense height, its nave-like space defined by two rows of heat-blackened granite pillars channeling rivers of molten rock in carved troughs along either wall. The vaulted ceiling is perpetually obscured by rising heat-haze and old soot. Upper galleries of ironwork cage anvil-platforms on multiple tiers. Every surface is scarred with hammer-marks and layered scale. The heat presses like a physical wall.

A ritual summoning hall with a vast circular pentagram inlaid in silver wire across a black-marble floor, its lines worn at the crossing points. Five altar-niches are cut into the curving walls, each holding remnants of centuries-old offerings reduced to dust and dark residue. Rune-carved pillars ring the circle. The vaulted ceiling is painted with layered summoning-diagrams in flaking red and gold pigment.

A long banquet hall with parallel trestle tables of age-blackened oak stretching the full length of the chamber beneath a hammerbeam ceiling of immense span. Four great hearths line each long wall, their stones smoke-darkened to charcoal. Rows of hanging iron chandeliers carry hundreds of candles. Tapestries between the hearths depict hunting scenes, their colors faded to dusky rose and grey.

A war-council chamber centered on a massive relief-map table of carved stone, its topographic surface stained with old ink markings and worn smooth at the edges where hands have leaned across campaigns. Banner-rows of conquered and allied houses hang from a low coffered ceiling. Arrow-slit windows in deep embrasures admit thin bars of cold light. The flagstone floor is tracked with countless boot-scuffs.

A portal hall of vaulted stone, its long axis lined on both sides with seven permanent archway-portals, each sealed with shimmering curtains of solidified light gone cloudy and cracked at the margins with disuse. The floor between them is worn into shallow trenches by centuries of crossing feet. Brass plaques above each arch are tarnished beyond easy reading. The ceiling vaults high and dark.

A magical temple-basilica with soaring nave walls carved floor-to-ceiling in dense interlocking rune-text, the letters packed so tightly they form a visual texture of ancient stone script. Floating stone rings, now motionless, hang at intervals down the central axis. Enormous candle-trees of black iron cluster at the apse. A cracked rose-window of deep violet and gold fills the west wall, its lead caming sagging.

A grand colonnade gallery connecting two palace wings, its long barrel-vaulted ceiling coffered in faded painted panels. Paired columns of veined grey marble line both sides, their bases worn to oval smoothness. Between each column pair hangs a portrait of an ancient ruler in a heavy gilt frame gone dark with age-varnish. The mosaic floor runner, once vivid, has paled to a soft blurred repetition of laurel.

A vast arcane basilica with a nave wide enough to lose perspective, its clerestory windows sending colored light down through centuries of accumulated dust-haze. The floor is a single continuous mosaic of the known world, its geography worn featureless near the entrance where foot-traffic has concentrated for generations. Rows of massive stone reading-lecterns line the aisles, each chained with iron book-locks long since broken open.

A royal coronation hall of immense breadth, its pointed barrel vault carried on responds of clustered columns rising from a floor of alternating black and white marble squares. At the far end a raised platform of three steps holds an empty gilded throne beneath a canopy of carved stone. The canopy's painted interior has faded to ghost-imagery. Cracked heraldic shields tile the upper walls in two continuous rows.

A cloistered inner courtyard wrapped on all sides by a pointed arcade of slender paired columns, their capitals carved with foliage now moss-softened. The enclosed garden at center has grown unkempt, low hedge-forms collapsed to shapeless mounds. A round pool at the center holds dark still water. Above, a vaulted glass roof of leaded diamond-panes, many replaced with plain grey glass where the colored originals broke.

A treasury vault-corridor of immense length, its groin-vaulted ceiling dropping in repeated arches above a floor of wide stone flags cracked unevenly by settling. Iron-banded vault-doors line both walls at close intervals, their locks enormous and furred with rust. Wall-sconces hold burned-down candle-stubs. The air is cold and dense with the smell of old metal. Scratched inventory marks in chalk ghost every door-frame.

A ceremonial stairwell of palace scale, three flights wide, its first landing breaking into twin symmetrical arms that return upward around a central open well. Marble newel statues of armored figures guard each turn, their faces worn soft by hands that have steadied on them for generations. Hanging iron chandeliers descend the full height. The risers are pale marble, each tread concave from use.

A spell-hall with a vast circular floor of black stone carrying a permanent summoning circle in inlaid silver, the metal raised and bright at the outer ring but worn nearly flush at center. Side-altars in arched recesses hold melted candle-architecture of extraordinary depth. The domed ceiling above is covered in dense astrological fresco, smoke-darkened across its lower reaches, clearer at the summit where a gilded eye remains vivid.

A long feasting hall of a dragonlord's mountain keep, its ceiling lost in smoke-shadow above a double row of massive timber trusses. Iron torch-rings the width of cartwheel crowd the walls. A single table of stone runs the full length, its surface stained with centuries of feasts. At the far end an enormous carved hearth occupies the full wall, its firebox tall enough to walk upright inside.
